To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed an evolutionary algorithm for the design of peptidic mimotopes that is based on a Pareto-based approach.
the Pareto-based multiobjectivization of the peptide design problem is a promising strategy for the automated design and optimization of peptidic mimotopes.
we have developed an in silico design method for peptidic mimotopes that are short and conformationally stable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of peptidic mimotopes, which are short peptides that mimic protein epitope binding sites.
the design of peptides with a high degree of specificity, short length, and conformational stability.
the automated design of effective peptic drugs.

the method presented here allows for the in silico design of peptidic mimics of protein epitopes that (a) are conformational stable, (b) are of short length, and (c ) mimic the antibody epitope of the protein thrombin and blood clotting factor VIII, respectively.
the method presented is a promising approach to design effective peptidomimetic drug candidates.
the proposed approach is a promising method for in silico mimotope design.

our method is a powerful tool for the design of peptidic mimotopes.
the proposed method is able to generate peptides that mimic the antibody epitopes, are conformationally rigid, and are short.
the multiobjective evolutionary algorithm is able to design short peptides that mimic the antibody epitope and that have low flexibility.

the method is able to find a set of solutions that are optimal in the design space, which we show by comparison with the best known solutions from the literature.
the method is able to generate peptides that satisfy multiple design objectives simultaneously.
multiobjective evolutionary algorithms are a promising method for the design of peptides with several objectives.
